headings.title: Driver's license deposit in lieu of bail for traffic offenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits arrested traffic offender, at mutual discretion of bail officer and driver, to deposit driver's license in lieu of bail, excluding DWI, leaving scene, suspended/revoked license, or fatal accident charges.

headings.title: Fifty-dollar bond alternative to driver's license deposit
headings.reviewNote: Permits arrested driver to decline license deposit and instead deposit a fifty-dollar bond per traffic offense, with officer receipt and deposit with court.

headings.title: Receipt issuance and driving authorization pending appearance
headings.reviewNote: Requires acceptance of bond or license, issuance of director-approved receipt allowing motor vehicle operation under section 302.181 until appearance, and new receipt upon continuance.

headings.title: Notice to director of revenue upon failure to appear
headings.reviewNote: Requires court clerk or judge to notify director of revenue within ten days of failure to appear, directing director to withhold license renewal or duplicate until final judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 7-01-92; removed unstated 'cash' qualifier from subsection 2 title and verified traffic bail deposit, receipt driving authority, and 10-day failure-to-appear notice.

headings.title: Fresh pursuit into state by out-of-state peace officers
headings.reviewNote: Grants out-of-state peace officers in fresh pursuit for felonies, DWI, or excessive BAC reciprocal authority to arrest and hold in custody in Missouri.

headings.title: Presentment before judge, lawfulness hearing, and extradition commitment
headings.reviewNote: Requires arresting officer without unnecessary delay to take arrested person before a county judge of competent jurisdiction for a lawfulness hearing, leading to extradition commitment/bail or discharge.

headings.title: Preservation of otherwise lawful arrests in this state
headings.reviewNote: Provides that subsection 1 shall not be construed to make unlawful any arrest in Missouri that would otherwise be lawful.

headings.title: Definition of state to include District of Columbia
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'state' to include the District of Columbia for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Definition of fresh pursuit for felonies and DWI
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'fresh pursuit' to include common-law fresh pursuit and pursuit without unreasonable delay of persons reasonably suspected of felonies, DWI, or excessive BAC.

headings.title: Short title citation as Uniform Law on Fresh Pursuit
headings.reviewNote: Permits citation of this section as the Uniform Law on Fresh Pursuit.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 6 subsections and statutory history; corrected 4 consecutive shifted subsections (#3–#6) and expanded subsection 2 title so all 6 headings match the Uniform Law on Fresh Pursuit text.

headings.title: Statewide arrest authority during fresh pursuit by certified peace officers
headings.reviewNote: Grants chapter 590 certified officers, conservation agents, capitol police, college/university police, and state park rangers statewide arrest authority during fresh pursuit initiated within their jurisdiction until contact is lost.

headings.title: Disposition of prisoner and court appearance following fresh pursuit arrest
headings.reviewNote: Directs prisoner disposition under warrant, uniform traffic ticket, or forthwith presentment before a judge for warrantless arrests (with section 544.455 release authority), unless officer issues a summons.

headings.title: Definition of fresh pursuit including suspected felonies and ordinance violations
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'fresh pursuit' as instant pursuit, including common-law hot pursuit and pursuit for suspected felonies, in-presence offenses/ordinance violations, or criminal arrest warrants.

headings.title: Minimum supervisory and safety policy standards for vehicular pursuits
headings.reviewNote: Requires public agencies electing to institute vehicular pursuits to adopt a safety policy meeting four minimum standards on supervision, vehicle count, coordination, and initiation/termination guidelines.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and statutory history; statewide fresh-pursuit arrest powers for listed certified officers, prisoner disposition, instant-pursuit definition, and agency vehicular-pursuit policy standards verified.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour discharge deadline for warrantless arrests
headings.reviewNote: Requires discharge of persons arrested and confined without warrant within twenty-four hours unless charged on oath of a credible person and held by warrant.

headings.title: Right of confinee to consult with counsel or representatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires permitting confinees at any reasonable time to consult with counsel or other persons acting on their behalf.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalties for unlawful detention or denial of counsel
headings.reviewNote: Makes refusal to release, denial of counsel, transfer, or false charging with intent to evade this section a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, 4 cross-references, and 6 case annotations; note catchline retains legacy 'twenty hours' phrasing while body subsection 1 sets a 24-hour warrantless detention limit, with counsel access and class A misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Definitions of body cavity search and strip search
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'body cavity search' and 'strip search' for sections 544.193 to 544.197.

headings.title: Probable cause requirement for strip searches in nonfelony arrests
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits strip or body cavity searches of persons arrested or detained for traffic or nonfelony offenses absent probable cause of concealed weapon, crime evidence, or contraband.

headings.title: Same-sex personnel and privacy requirements for strip searches
headings.reviewNote: Requires same-sex personnel and private premises out of view for all strip and body cavity searches, while allowing a readily available person present at the searched person's request and consent.

headings.title: Warrant and medical personnel for nonfelony body cavity searches
headings.reviewNote: Requires a duly executed search warrant, sanitary conditions, and a licensed physician, registered nurse, or practical nurse for nonfelony or traffic body cavity searches.

headings.title: Written command authorization and written report requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires advance written authorization from the agency commander and a written report containing listed details furnished to the person searched.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections and statutory history; refined subsection 4 title to preserve nonfelony/traffic scope for body cavity search warrants and verified definitions, probable cause, privacy, and command authorization rules.

headings.title: Preservation of common law and statutory rights and criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Preserves common-law and statutory damages or injunctive rights and criminal prosecution of officials violating sections 544.193 to 544.197.

headings.title: Private civil action for actual damages, punitive damages, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Permits a person suffering actual damage from a violation of sections 544.193 to 544.197 to bring a civil action for actual damages, discretionary punitive damages and equitable relief, and reasonable prevailing-party attorney's fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; preservation of common-law/statutory remedies and criminal liability plus private civil action for actual/punitive damages, equitable relief, and prevailing-party attorney fees verified.

headings.title: Pretrial release on personal recognizance and authorized conditional release terms
headings.reviewNote: Permits pretrial release on personal recognizance or any combination of seven listed conditions (including supervision, travel limits, bond, ten-percent deposit, or electronic monitoring with county-commission cost rule) to reasonably assure appearance.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining pretrial release conditions
headings.reviewNote: Directs judge to consider listed factors including offense nature, weight of evidence, family/community ties, financial resources, mental condition, convictions, and appearance/flight history.

headings.title: Release order, statement of conditions, and violation warnings
headings.reviewNote: Requires judge authorizing release to issue an appropriate order stating conditions, inform defendant of violation penalties, and advise that an arrest warrant will issue immediately upon violation.

headings.title: Prompt review of release conditions after twenty-four-hour detention
headings.reviewNote: Entitles a person still detained after twenty-four hours due to inability to meet release conditions to prompt review upon application to the imposing judge.

headings.title: Judicial amendment and modification of release conditions
headings.reviewNote: Permits judge at any time to amend release order to impose additional or different conditions, triggering subsection 4 review if detention or part-time custody results.

headings.title: Inapplicability of formal rules of evidence to pretrial release hearings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that information stated or offered in connection with release orders need not conform to formal rules of evidence.

headings.title: Disposition by forfeiture of collateral security unimpaired
headings.reviewNote: Preserves court-authorized disposition of cases by forfeiture of collateral security.

headings.title: Application of release standards to municipal ordinance violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipal judges to release persons charged with municipal ordinance violations under the same conditions and manner as associate circuit judges.

headings.title: Local court rules authorizing pretrial electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Permits circuit courts to adopt local rules authorizing pretrial electronic monitoring under subsection 1(6) in lieu of incarceration for specified offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 9 subsections, statutory history, and 1976 State v. Adams annotation; removed unstated 'Written' from subsection 3 title and verified personal recognizance, conditional release terms, 24-hour review, and local electronic-monitoring rules.

headings.title: Short title citation as Sam Pratt's Law
headings.reviewNote: Establishes short title citation as 'Sam Pratt's Law'.

headings.title: Condition prohibiting compensated child care services in child abuse cases
headings.reviewNote: Permits court in cases involving child abuse, neglect, or death to prohibit compensated child care as a section 544.455 release condition, requiring notice of determination and final disposition to DHSS and DSS.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; Sam Pratt's Law short title and permissive release condition prohibiting compensated child care in child abuse, neglect, or death cases verified.

headings.title: Commitment to county jail upon nonbailable offense or unmet release conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires commitment to county jail until discharged by due course of law if offense is nonbailable, electronic monitoring is not granted, or section 544.455 release conditions are unmet.

headings.title: Presumption of flight risk and commitment for unlawfully present aliens
headings.reviewNote: Creates rebuttable statutory presumption against release under section 544.455 when judge reasonably believes defendant is an unlawfully present alien (note 2016 Lopez-Matias v. State constitutional annotation in source notes).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 2016 Lopez-Matias v. State annotation (holding wholesale bail denial for defendants unable to prove lawful presence violates Mo. Const. Art. I, § 20); both titles verified neutrally against statutory text.

headings.title: Immigration status verification within forty-eight hours through federal center
headings.reviewNote: Requires arresting agency within forty-eight hours to query DHS Law Enforcement Support Center when jailed prisoner's nationality or lawful status cannot be verified from documents or reasonable effort, and notify DHS if unlawful.

headings.title: Preservation of bond eligibility and release rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section shall be construed to deny bond or prevent release of an otherwise eligible person.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, transfer note (formerly 577.680), and effective date 1-01-17; 48-hour LESC immigration verification query and preservation of bond/release eligibility verified.

headings.title: Crime of failure to appear while released on bond or recognizance
headings.reviewNote: Makes knowingly failing to appear before a court or judicial officer while released on recognizance or bond the crime of failure to appear in addition to security forfeiture.

headings.title: Classification of failure to appear based on underlying charge severity
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to appear as a class E felony, class A misdemeanor, or infraction (with municipal fine cap) based on the underlying criminal or municipal charge.

headings.title: Preservation of inherent judicial contempt powers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in sections 544.040 to 544.665 prevents any court from exercising its power to punish for contempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 1-01-17; knowing failure to appear offense, tiered felony/misdemeanor/infraction classifications, and judicial contempt preservation verified.

headings.title: Bail denial or protective conditions upon showing of danger to victim or community
headings.reviewNote: Permits court to deny bail or impose appropriate protective conditions upon state showing that defendant poses a danger to a crime victim, witness, or the community.

headings.title: Evidence and considerations in assessing dangerousness
headings.reviewNote: Permits court in assessing dangerousness to consider all relevant evidence including criminal record, probation/bail status at time of offense, and crime circumstances.

headings.title: Right to trial within one hundred twenty days of arraignment upon bail denial
headings.reviewNote: Entitles defendant denied bail for dangerousness, upon written request filed at arraignment, to trial within 120 days of arraignment or venue-change order (whichever is later), waived by defendant continuance or bail setting.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and statutory history; permissive bail denial or protective conditions upon dangerousness showing, evidentiary considerations, and 120-day trial right upon written arraignment request verified.
